title: Oscar and the Wolf
premise: Wendell Amberdale, a nonbinary gatekeeper hiding a wild, inherited magic they barely understand, has kept the Thornfell gate sealed for years — the last ward against the wolf-spirits their grandmother once bargained with. When the crown's witch-hunt sweeps the mountains and a wounded fugitive named Sera collapses at Wendell's door carrying half of a broken seal-stone, Wendell learns the gate is already failing and that their own blood is the key to both locking it forever or opening it. Hunted by inquisitor Captain Rell and shadowed by the wolf-spirit Oscar, who claims to have known their grandmother, Wendell must choose between destroying their inheritance and claiming it. In the end, Wendell takes the wolf's bargain on their own terms: they become the new keeper bound into the gate itself, sealing it from within while sending Sera away with the truth — alive, changed, and no longer entirely human.
about_author: Odile Oyelaran is a fantasy writer raised between a lighthouse town and her grandmother's mountain village, where stories about doors that should stay shut were bedtime staples. She writes about outsiders who inherit burdens they never asked for, and she insists every wolf in her books deserves a fair trial.

chapters.title: The Gate That Should Stay Shut
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A quiet morning routine at the Thornfell gate establishes their solitary life, their hidden gift, and the strange warmth the old stones give off when they touch them. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness with an undercurrent of dread.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Crossroads
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In the valley market, a crown herald announces a bounty on anyone with 'the old gift.' Wendell watches a neighbor's son dragged away in chains. Emotional beat: fear crystallizing into resolve to hide deeper.

chapters.title: Sera at the Door
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A bleeding stranger, Sera, collapses at the gatehouse clutching half a shattered stone that hums like the gate itself. Wendall breaks their own rule and lets her in. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: Half a Seal
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She reveals she stole the stone fragment from the crown's own vaults; it is half of the seal binding the wolf-gates, and it answers Wendell's touch. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering you are part of something ancient.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Bargained
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Searching the attic, Wendell finds their grandmother's journal describing a pact with the wolf-spirits — and a name: Oscar. The gate shudders that night. Emotional beat: grief tangled with betrayal by a dead ancestor.

chapters.title: Captain Rell
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. The inquisitor interrogates villagers, cold and methodical, and finds a witness who saw light at the gatehouse. He begins the climb. Emotional beat: chilling certainty; the hunter who believes he is righteous.

chapters.title: Oscar
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A wolf with human eyes appears inside the wards, unbothered by them, and speaks: he knew Grandmother Amberdale, and the failing gate will drown the valleys in what sleeps behind it. Emotional beat: terror and terrible fascination.

chapters.title: Three Days to Thornfell
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera urges flight south with the fragment; Wendell refuses to abandon the gate. They argue through smugglers' roads as Rell's riders close in. Emotional beat: fracturing trust between two people who need each other.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. To buy passage through a hidden pass, Wendell uses a sliver of their gift before witnesses — including one who sells them out. Emotional beat: the first true price of survival paid.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They return to find the gatehouse burned and Rell waiting among the ruins with irons forged to dampen magic. Wendell surrenders so Sera can flee. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered out of love not yet admitted.

chapters.title: Irons
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Caged and damped, Wendell endures Rell's interrogation, learning the crown wants the seal-stone to open the gates deliberately and weaponize the wolves. Emotional beat: despair transmuting into fury.

chapters.title: The Wolf in the Walls
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera, guided by Oscar, infiltrates the prison convoy camp; the spirit passes through stone and iron as if they were mist. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance with a creature whose motives are unreadable.

chapters.title: Bargain in the Dark
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Oscar offers Wendell escape and the full truth of the inheritance — but names his price: a keeper must bind themselves to the gate willingly, and he intends it to be Wendell. Emotional beat: the horror of a choice dressed as a gift.

chapters.title: Flight Through Thornfell
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The rescue goes wrong; Sera kills a soldier to save Wendell and carries the guilt of it. They flee into the high passes with Rell hunting. Emotional beat: trauma shared in silence, drawing them closer.

chapters.title: The Second Fragment
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Following grandmother's journal, they reach a shrine where the other half of the seal was hidden — and find Rell already there, having read the same pages captured from the house. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Steel and Stone
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Battle at the shrine: Sera holds soldiers off, Oscar tears through the line, and Wendell seizes both fragments as the gate behind them begins to crack audibly across the mountains. Emotional beat: chaos, adrenaline, irreversible commitment.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Touching the joined fragments, Wendell experiences the gate's memory: centuries of keepers, the original war, and the truth that Oscar was once a man who made the same choice. Emotional beat: awe and mourning; understanding the price fully at last.

chapters.title: Rell's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. Confronted with the gate opening and the wolves' true nature, Rell must choose between his orders and the annihilation they would cause. He turns his blade on his own superiors' messenger. Emotional beat: a zealot breaking — redemption bought too late to be clean.

chapters.title: The Choosing
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the cracking gate, Wendell rejects both options offered — destruction of the gift or Oscar's binding — and instead rewrites the pact: they will enter the gate as its living keeper, but on terms of their own naming, with Sera as anchor to the outside. Emotional beat: agency seized from fate itself.

chapters.title: Into the Stone
chapters.summary: Alternating Wendell and Sera POVs. The binding: Wendell steps into the gate as it seals, becoming voice and ward both; Sera speaks the anchor-words, weeping, holding the connection open just enough. Emotional beat: heartbreak transfigured into covenant.

chapters.title: After the Wolf
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Spring returns to Thornfell. Sera keeps the gatehouse, tells travelers true stories, and each dusk hears Wendell's voice in the stones — present, changed, at peace. Emotional beat: grief settled into devotion.

chapters.title: Oscar and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, final chapter. Inside the gate, Wendell walks beside Oscar through the long memory of the mountain, two keepers keeping watch together, as somewhere above a child touches the warm stone and feels it answer. Emotional beat: quiet, earned transcendence.
